    src/Connector.Infrastructure/DataSources/PostgreSql

    Layer infrastructure · project Connector.Infrastructure

    Project navigation: Connector.Infrastructure

    Key components

    Component Kind Used by Summary
    PostgreSqlDialect class 2 ISqlDialect for PostgreSQL — the single home of every PostgreSQL-specific fragment the generic query builders emit: double-quote identifier quoting, @pN parameter placeholders (Npgsql's named-parameter syntax), LIMIT n, ::text casts, = ANY(@array), IS NOT DISTINCT FROM, string_agg, and how a PostgreSQL text value maps to JSON (PostgreSqlJsonValues). Stateless; use Instance.
    CompiledPostgreSqlQuery record 1 A SourceQuery compiled to PostgreSQL: SQL text plus the positional-named (@p0, @p1, …) parameters it references.
    PostgreSqlJsonValues class 1 Turns a PostgreSQL value in its text output format into the JSON value PostgreSQL's own to_json would produce for it — so the export tree engine can assemble JSON in C# that is identical to what the database would build with json_build_object. Follows to_json's type categories: smallint/integer/bigint/real/double precision/numeric → a JSON number with the exact same digits (NaN/Infinity stay strings, as in Postgres);boolean → true/false; json/jsonb → embedded as JSON;date → unchanged; timestamp/timestamptz → ISO 8601 with a T separator and a ±HH:MM offset;arrays → JSON arrays, element by element (nested arrays nest);everything else (text, uuid, time, interval, enums, …) → a JSON string of the text as-is. Assumes the server's default DateStyle (ISO), which is what makes date/timestamp text ISO-shaped. Composite (row) types and types with a custom cast to json aren't special-cased — they come out as strings; no exported column in this codebase uses either.
    PostgreSqlQueryCompiler class 1 Compiles the database-neutral SourceQuery into PostgreSQL — the only place that model meets a SQL dialect. Validates against the given SourceSchema first (SourceQueryValidator), so every identifier emitted is one the schema reported, double-quoted by PostgreSqlDialect, and table aliases are synthetic (t0, t1, …). No caller-supplied text other than those identifiers and output aliases ever becomes SQL: every filter value is a bound parameter, and Limit is an Int32 rendered by the dialect.
    PostgreSqlDataSourceProvider class 0 The IDataSourceProvider for PostgreSql. Owns every piece of PostgreSQL-specific connection/schema/query logic: building an Npgsql connection string, introspecting information_schema, and executing a caller-built SQL query generically. Registered as a singleton (see Program.cs) — it holds no per-call state; every method opens and disposes its own NpgsqlConnection.

    Member Summary Derived from code Complexity
    OpenConnectionAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) An open ADO.NET connection for callers that need more than one query per call — the import path's multi-statement transaction. The caller disposes it. 2
    ValidateConfig(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) Whether config has what this provider needs to connect (required fields, a valid TLS mode or instance URL): a user-facing message, or null when it's usable. Checked before any connection attempt; the only place per-source-type config rules live. 1
    TargetHost(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) The host a connection with the (validated) config reaches — what the SSRF check in POST /api/connection resolves. 1
    IsAlwaysEncrypted(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) True when config can only ever reach the source encrypted — never falling back to plaintext. 1
    BuildConnectionString(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig) 3
    TestConnectionAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Opens a connection and reads its schema; never throws for a reachability/credential failure — that's reported via Failed instead, sanitized of any connection-string/credential detail by Detail (Npgsql can echo the offending connection string, password included, back inside an exception message). 2
    ReadSchemaAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Reads the live schema (tables/columns/PK/FK) of the data source described by config. Throws on failure — unlike TestConnectionAsync, this is called once a connection is already known-good and a failure here is a real, reportable error. 1
    ExecuteAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DataSources.SourceQuery, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Compiles query with PostgreSqlQueryCompiler against the live schema (read fresh on every call, so a column dropped since a definition was saved is reported as unknown rather than failing inside Postgres) and executes it — same row materialization as ExecuteNativeAsync. 1
    ExecuteNativeAsync(Connector.Core.DataSources.DataSourceConfig, Connector.Core.DataSources.NativeSqlQuery, System.Threading.CancellationToken) Executes query's SQL generically: the provider does not parse or understand the text itself, only materializes rows. Date/timestamp columns are coerced to ISO-8601 (yyyy-MM-dd) the same way the pre-abstraction row-reading loop in DynamicExportService did, so every existing caller's output is unchanged. 4

    ConvertNativeTextToJson(string, string) Renders nativeText — a value in the backend's own text format, as returned for a ReturnNativeText query — as the JSON value the backend's own JSON encoding would give a column of type dataType (DataType): numbers as JSON numbers, booleans as JSON booleans, JSON columns embedded as JSON, arrays as JSON arrays, anything else as a string. 1
    FormatValue(object, string) The connector's string form of a non-null column value as the driver returned it, for a column the backend calls dataType: date/timestamp columns as yyyy-MM-dd, everything else the value's own ToString(). Shared by the provider's row materialization and the import walker, so old values read for a diff match exported values exactly. 5
    BuildStringAggregate(string, string) Aggregates expression (as text) over the rows of the enclosing SELECT into one string joined by delimiter; null values are skipped. 1
    BuildSetClause(string, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string>, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string?>, System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary<string, object?>) The SET clause (without the keyword) of an UPDATE on table that assigns each of columns the matching text value in values, converted by the backend to the column's own type. Binds the values into parameters (named from BuildParameterName, continuing at its current count). Used by the import releaser's updates. 1
    BuildInsertRow(string, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string>, System.Collections.Generic.IReadOnlyList<string?>, System.Collections.Generic.IDictionary<string, object?>) An INSERT of one row into table, setting each of columns to the matching text value in values, converted by the backend to the column's own type (uuid, date, number…). Binds the values into parameters (named from BuildParameterName, continuing at its current count). Used by the import releaser's root-row inserts. 1

    PostgreSqlJsonValues

    class · PostgreSqlJsonValues.cs

    Turns a PostgreSQL value in its text output format into the JSON value PostgreSQL's own to_json would produce for it — so the export tree engine can assemble JSON in C# that is identical to what the database would build with json_build_object. Follows to_json's type categories: smallint/integer/bigint/real/double precision/numeric → a JSON number with the exact same digits (NaN/Infinity stay strings, as in Postgres);boolean → true/false; json/jsonb → embedded as JSON;date → unchanged; timestamp/timestamptz → ISO 8601 with a T separator and a ±HH:MM offset;arrays → JSON arrays, element by element (nested arrays nest);everything else (text, uuid, time, interval, enums, …) → a JSON string of the text as-is. Assumes the server's default DateStyle (ISO), which is what makes date/timestamp text ISO-shaped. Composite (row) types and types with a custom cast to json aren't special-cased — they come out as strings; no exported column in this codebase uses either.
